correctness.rationale: For any positive period n, equality of Laurent principal ideals permutes the finite x-support by I ↦ A^n I − u. A power of that permutation fixes every support difference; no eigenvalue of A has modulus one, so the difference must be zero. The periodic primes are therefore precisely vertical primes, all fixed by F_r. On an infinite orbit only finitely many primes could be contracted by the birational marking. A block of contracted primes between noncontracted ones sends a divisor of X to a lower-dimensional center and then reappears as a divisor. The intermediate center must be in the indeterminacy of the corresponding further iterate, since a morphism there could not raise its dimension. The divisor criterion for NS stability rules this out. After removing the finitely many fixed contracted primes, codimension-one correspondence identifies all remaining torus primes with the primes of X off the inverse-exceptional boundary. Divisor localization thus gives the exact boundary sequence, with kernel generated freely by x_i, y_j and inverted vertical equations modulo constants, and Pic(X)=NS(X) since X is smooth projective rational. Pullback of an effective boundary divisor is effective and remains on the boundary: a nonboundary prime is a prime of the surviving open and its forward image is the corresponding nonboundary prime. The principal-divisor formula intertwines the kernel action A ⊕ I and the quotient NS action. Stability and birational invariance of the first dynamical degree give quotient spectral radius |α|; the boundary matrix consequently has spectral radius |α| and peripheral eigenvalue α. Perron–Frobenius forbids its phase: equality of powers of α and its conjugate would give a repeated root of a rational cubic, hence a rational repeated root and a rational integral third root β^m in (0,1). The example was independently checked by exact determinant evaluation for tI−A at t=−1,0,1,2 (values −3,−1,1,9), determinant 1, and cubic discriminant −31; sign and rational-root tests give the required irreducible spectral type. The uploaded example checker was inspected, not executed, and does not verify the assertion over all models.
residual_risks: The proof concerns divisor/NS stability on smooth projective complex models, not higher-codimension stability or arbitrary identity-product problems.
